accepted.question_text: For the disordered copolymer model whose critical curve satisfies h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ in the weak-coupling regime when α ∈ (0,1), determine the universal slope m_α as an explicit function of α. Equivalently, identify the weak-coupling asymptotic of the critical curve beyond the currently known bounds, using only the model data supported in the paper: α is the tail exponent in the renewal law K(n) ~ C_K / n^(1+α), h_c(λ) is the localization-delocalization critical curve, and m_α depends only on α and not on the detailed law of the disorder sequence or on the full renewal distribution.

evidence.quote: What the previous results and discussion expose is that a convincing heuristic theory predicting the location of the critical curve, or just its slope at the origin, is lacking. In this sense we consider that capturing the value of mα, for α ∈ (0,1), is an important open problem.

In fact, as more extensivily explained in section 4, for α ∈ (0,1) we have hc(λ) λ&0 ∼ mαλ, with mα > 0 depending only on α. The slope mα is therefore a universal feature of the model: it does not depend on the details of the disorder sequence ω and of the underlying renewal τ.
K(n) := P(τ1 = n) n→∞∼ CK / n 1+α, where α > 0 and CK > 0.

accepted.question_text: In the same weak-coupling copolymer setting, prove the strict lower bound m_1/2 > 2/3 for the universal slope m_α of the critical curve h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ when α = 1/2.

In fact, as more extensivily explained in section 4, for α ∈ (0,1) we have hc(λ) λ&0 ∼ mαλ, with mα > 0 depending only on α.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist any α > 0 for which the universal weak-coupling slope m_α of the copolymer critical curve equals 1/(1+α)? Here m_α is defined by h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ for small λ when the limit exists, and the question asks whether the lower-bound expression 1/(1+α) is ever the exact value of the slope for the original copolymer model.

evidence.quote: Since computing explicitly quenched quantities may be really out of reach, here are two sub-problems that are open: ? show that m1/2 > 2/3; ? is mα = 1/(1+α) for some α > 0?
It becomes therefore quite relevant to get a hold of the value of mα (at least for α ∈ (0,1)). As a matter of fact, from (17) one directly extracts 1/(1+α) ≤ mα ≤ 1, for every α > 0.

accepted.question_text: The paper proves that for every λ > 0 there exists c(λ) < ∞ such that F(λ, h_c(λ)+δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ^2 for every δ > 0, where F is the quenched free energy and h_c is the critical curve. Can this smoothing estimate be strengthened by replacing the power δ^2 with a strictly larger exponent, i.e. by proving that the free energy vanishes faster than quadratically as the critical point is approached from the localized side?

evidence.quote: for every λ > 0 there exists c(λ) < ∞ such that F(λ,hc(λ) +δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ 2 (20) for every δ > 0.
A natural open question however is: ? Can one improve (20), in the sense of replacing the exponent 2 with a larger value?

accepted.question_text: In the localized phase, let μ(λ,h) := -lim_{N→∞} (1/N) log E[(1 + exp(-2λ Σ_{n=1}^N (ω_n+h)))/Z_{N,ω}] and let F(λ,h) be the free energy. As h approaches the critical curve h_c(λ) from below, are the two quantities logarithmically equivalent in the sense that log μ(λ,h) ~ log F(λ,h)? This asks whether the decay scale controlling correlation length or longest-excursion asymptotics vanishes at the same logarithmic rate as the free energy near criticality.

evidence.quote: As expected, the rate of exponential decay of the correlation functions (or inverse correlation length), i.e. c2 in (36), tends to zero as h % hc(λ). In general, it is a very interesting open problem to understand the relation between this and the way the free energy vanishes close to the critical point.

But: ? is it true that logμ(λ,h) ∼ log F(λ,h) as h & hc(λ)? In view of the discussion on disorder relevance in section 1.5, we expect that this is not the case and establishing such a result would be very interesting.
where μ is defined as μ(λ,h) = − lim N→∞ 1/N logE 1+e −2λ ∑ N n=1 (ωn+h) / ZN,ω .

accepted.question_text: Fix parameters (λ,h) in the interior of the delocalized region D, where D = {(λ,h) : F(λ,h)=0}. Is it true that for every ε > 0, the quenched polymer measure of the event that the polymer stays entirely in the favorable solvent during the whole terminal segment [εN, N] tends to 0 almost surely as N → ∞? In the paper's notation this is the question whether lim_{N→∞} P_{N,ω}(Δ_n = 0 for every n ∈ [εN, N] ∩ N) = 0 almost surely, where Δ_n is the indicator that monomer n is below the interface, so Δ_n = 0 means that monomer n is not below the interface.

evidence.quote: However the nature of the delocalized phase, in the pathwise sense, is still very little understood and, notably, almost sure results are laking. For example: ? Is it true that, if (λ,h) is in the interior of D, for every ε > 0 we have limN→∞ PN,ω(Δn = 0 for every n ∈ [εN,N]∩N) = 0 P(dω)-almost surely?
Based on this, we say that (λ,h) ∈ D (delocalized regime) if F(λ,h) = 0, while (λ,h) ∈ L (localized regime) if F(λ,h) > 0.

The renewal τ identifies the polymer-interface contacts: we still need to know whether the excursion is above or below the axis. For this let ξ = {ξn}n∈N denote an IID sequence of B(1/2) variables ... Starting from the couple (τ,ξ ) we build a new sequence Δ = {Δn}n∈N by setting Δn = ∑ ∞ j=1 ξj 1(τ j−1,τ j ](n), in analogy with the simple random walk case: the signs Δn are constant between the points in τ and they are determined by ξ .
